purpose: Demonstrate automatic candidate combat windows derivable from D2 MIDI without hand-authored per-song beat charts.
runtime_status: No Godot runtime integration or gameplay balancing was implemented or claimed.

algorithm.input: 12 derived D2 MIDI files; only MIDI notes and embedded muscriptor bar-offset metadata are read.
algorithm.onset_rule: Positive-velocity note_on on channel 10 or a drum/percussion-named track; if none exist, use positive-velocity note_on from any track; zero velocity is excluded.
algorithm.simultaneous_rule: Merge note-ons whose integrated MIDI onset times are within 0.020s into one candidate; retain pitch/count provenance.
algorithm.minimum_spacing_rule: Greedy chronological thinning with a 0.180s global minimum center gap.
algorithm.long_gap_fallback_rule: Between available events, insert quarter-note tempo-map candidates while a gap exceeds max(1.25s, 3.0 local quarter-note durations). If no note-ons exist, use a tempo quarter grid across the file.
algorithm.window_rule: Half-width=min(0.090s, 0.30*left interval, 0.30*right interval); clipped to nominal game-audio bounds.
algorithm.time_rule: Integrate the full effective MIDI tempo map in tick order; then subtract the embedded muscriptor:bar_offset seconds. Same-tick tempo uses last track/message order.
algorithm.neutrality: No manual time signatures, section labels, guessed accents, or forced J/K key sequence; drum pitches and MIDI velocity are provenance only.
algorithm.confidence_meaning: Labels identify the evidence type, not a calibrated probability or proof of audible alignment.

midi_test_02_interval_example.interpretation: Intervals follow selected MIDI drum-family onsets and are not a fixed 130 BPM quarter-note grid; event pitch families are retained for inspection, not labeled as true accents.

limitations: This is an offline algorithm demonstration, not Godot runtime code. It does not prove that player input, pause, latency compensation, or game-state transitions are implemented.
MIDI note-on metadata may not match audible attacks; the nominal trim transform does not measure remaining render, decoder, device, or human-perception delay.
180 ms spacing, 20 ms merging, fallback thresholds, and 90 ms maximum window half-width are experimental global parameters, not play-tested or balanced values.
Drum pitch and velocity have no asserted semantic role, loudness, or true accent meaning. The algorithm does not impose J/K alternation or any key assignment.
Tempo-quarter fallback creates candidate timing only; it does not claim a note-on or musical accent at that point.
